sanskrit_verse:
साक्ष्य उद्दिष्टो यदि प्रेयाद् गच्छेद् वापि दिगन्तरम्
तच्छ्रोतारः प्रमाणं स्युः प्रमाणं ह्य् उत्तरक्रिया
transliteration:
sākṣya uddiṣṭo yadi preyād gacched vāpi digantaram
tacchrotāraḥ pramāṇaṃ syuḥ pramāṇaṃ hy uttarakriyā
sph_interpretive_translation: When a witness departs to another region, whether nearby or distant, those who hear his testimony become the evidence; evidence indeed is the basis of subsequent action.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates from direct experiential transmission
Causation follows the chain of conscious witnessing
Capacity-based responsibility lies in the recipient's ability to uphold truth
Restoration logic requires continuity of witnessed dharma
Consciousness alignment occurs through unbroken pramāṇa
executable_legal_axioms: IF witness departs to any spatial boundary THEN hearing recipients inherit evidentiary capacity
IF pramāṇa is transmitted THEN subsequent action MUST align with witnessed truth
IF conscious capacity is present THEN responsibility transfers automatically without punitive condition
IF testimony chain remains unbroken THEN legal consequence flows by ontological necessity
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, when primary witnesses are relocated or displaced, the burden of evidence shifts to those who have received the testimony directly. The court must recognize that pramāṇa does not diminish with spatial movement but continues through conscious reception. The threshold of responsibility is determined not by proximity but by capacity to sustain and transmit witnessed truth.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa functions as causal substrate wherein action unfolds sequentially through conscious receivership. There is no punitive framework here—only sequential manifestation of dharma through those capable of sustaining it. Responsibility arises naturally where capacity exists, ensuring proportional alignment without imposition of suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process by verifying uninterrupted transmission of testimony
Activate responsibility assumption protocol among qualified hearers
Restore integrity through reaffirmation of witnessed truth in current context
Realign consciousness via collective acknowledgment of pramāṇa continuity
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. Witnessing establishes pramāṇa; action proceeds thereby. No punishment arises—only restoration through conscious continuity. Reality is non-punitive; consciousness is the ultimate adjudicator.
